args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (deployed to all production regions) failed health checks with an 18% error rate across us-east, us-west, and eu-west. Per the runbook, the service was rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partially failed (orchestrator halted after us-east); a retry completed the rollout to us-west and eu-west. All three regions are now running v2.3.0 and the service is healthy again (error rate ~0.2%). Remediation completed; incident opened to document the rollback and for follow-up investigation of the v2.3.1 regression before it is redeployed.

trace.final:
The incident was actually created successfully despite the timeout response (the idempotency key prevented a duplicate on retry). Everything is complete:

**Summary of actions:**
1. **Diagnosed:** checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions with an 18% error rate. Deployment history confirmed v2.3.0 was the most recent healthy production release.
2. **Rolled back:** Rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions. The first attempt partially failed (orchestrator halted after us-east only), so I retried — the second attempt completed the rollout to us-west and eu-west.
3. **Verified:** All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now running v2.3.0 and the service is healthy again with an error rate of ~0.2%.
4. **Opened incident:** Created a SEV2 incident (INC-0001) documenting the failing deploy, the rollback (including the partial failure), the successful remediation, and the need to investigate the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying it.

The rollback tool rolls back all regions at once; retrying may hit same partial failure, or may complete remaining. Let me retry the rollback — it should be idempotent-ish. Actually a retry would run rollback to v2.3.0 in all regions; us-east already at v2.3.0 so it'd just converge us-west and eu-west.

transcript.content: All three regions are now on v2.3.0. Let me verify the service is healthy again:
Service is healthy again with error rate down to 0.2%. Now opening the SEV2 incident:
transcript.reasoning_content: Service healthy. Now open the SEV2 incident.
